name: Darrell
statement: Figuring out how things should work — and whether designing them is what I want to do.
questions: Is design — working out what something should be — what I actually want to do?
Which parts of making something should I not hand to AI?
What changes when I make something for a real person, not just for myself?
about:
I'm studying Information Systems at SMU. The degree isn't about design, so this site is where I explore it in my own time.

In poly, UX design and front-end web development came easily to me — far more easily than maths. I like working out what something should be, solving the problem, and ending up with something you can actually use. I've also noticed I don't enjoy code for its own sake.

So this is a direction I'm choosing to explore seriously, not a title I've earned. The site is the record: what I make, what I try, and how my thinking changes. Every few months I write a checkpoint asking whether it's still the direction.

I'm exploring AI the same way — until I can confidently say I use it as a tool.
background: Information Systems at SMU. Before that, poly.

title: The property agent site
desc: A website for a Singapore property agent — the one project I've finished. Write-up to come.

title: Bloomberger Terminal
desc: A Bloomberg-inspired web app powered by free and low-cost market APIs. React + Vite, with a dark editorial aesthetic that makes dense data feel calm.

title: Website Factory
desc: An idea for a multi-agent pipeline that generates websites for Singapore property agents. I barely started it.
standing: I went for automation before I had done the work once by hand. The one property agent site I did finish, I made by going back and forth with Claude instead.

title: Ember
desc: A hobby-discovery app — private by design, real-world by intention. A warm amber aesthetic wrapped around a "today's spark" home screen that nudges you offline.

title: Touching Earth
desc: An all-in-one trip companion — itinerary, bookings, packing lists, expense splitting, and the logistics that usually live in five different apps, in one.

title: Fencing Ranking
desc: The official rankings platform for Fencing Singapore — a public leaderboard on one side, and on the other, the admin backbone running competitions, points configuration, high-performance tracking, and finance.

title: Macro
desc: A personal trading system — screens for swing setups against a rule-based strategy and logs every trade to prove out whether it actually works, plus a macro calendar, research feed, and a retirement calculator to chart the way out.

title: Smart Contract Builder
desc: A Figma-style drag-and-drop Solidity generator. Visual logic in, deployable contracts out.

title: Site Ecosystem
desc: Interconnected apps for contracts, approvals, VOs, and BIM — one source of truth for on-site teams.

title: Seiko Catalogue
desc: A dark, luxury editorial catalogue app. A proof of concept for curated watch discovery.

title: What to Eat
desc: A decision engine for your next meal — factoring in as much personal data as it can, so the suggestion sounds like it came from you, not a random wheel.

title: A small dithering study
summary: Ordered dither, error diffusion, halftone and noise — a canvas tool to see what each technique does to an image, including your own photo.

title: Repeatability: same prompt, two runs
summary: Asked Claude for the same property agent landing page twice, to see how much the output actually varies.
